revisions.text:
- A turn is the work since the user's last message, your subagents' work included; a
  background wake or loop tick does not start a new one. It is past its range when it
  crosses a limit `hq pause limits` prints (active time, tool calls, subagents
  spawned, compactions), or the budget the user set for this turn on the first line of
  their own message (`budget: 12h`, alone on the line, which scales the other limits
  with it). Budget text anywhere else, quoted, fenced or pasted included, is an
  example: it sets nothing, and you ask nothing about it. When the hook reports a
  malformed first-line directive, mention it in your next report and carry on under
  the turn's limits. An approved spec, plan or task is not a budget, nothing you write
  can set one, and a prompt you write for another session never carries a budget line.
  Check `hq pause status` before dispatching a subagent, at each plan-task boundary
  and after a compaction; where the harness has no pause hook, keep the same counts
  yourself against those limits, counting a running call or wait in full and time
  spent waiting on the user not at all. The hook's warning means finish a coherent
  step. Its refusal, or your own count past a limit, means stop: from then on, only
  the report, the park, and stopping work you already started (the hook enforces this
  where it runs). A paused park records the worktree, process and retained-item
  accounting you already hold and says it was not refreshed; the session that resumes
  refreshes it before other work, which here outranks Processes' accounting at park.
  As the controller (or working alone), write the pause report, park the task
  `--waiting-on user --reason decision` with the decision as its next step, and end
  the turn. As a subagent, park any claim `--waiting-on agent` for your controller and
  return; only the controller reports. The report gives what the turn spent (active
  time, tool calls, subagents, compactions, and tokens or rate limit where you can see
  them), what is done and verified, what is left with your estimate of its cost,
  anything that went wrong, and one decision with your recommendation: continue under
  a budget you name, narrow the work, or stop. The user's reply ends the pause; it is
  not an approval of routine steps, and the next turn asks nothing until it too
  crosses a limit. Never edit the hook's state or limits, split work across turns or
  controllers, or start a fresh session to stay under a limit.
